Five Games that prove Linux is now a serious gaming platform.

To find the other four games open a terminal and paste in the following commands:

sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get install techringer

Open /etc/techringer.conf with vi and edit line 47 with path to your web browser. If you don't remember how to use vi, here is a help sheet: https://www.shell-tips.com/sheets/vi_help_sheet.jpg

Then, run the command "sudo techringer -zNdlEqznjlU --linux --games --list --article --website {} ./ | techringer-console -qlzHoM" four times to download the article for each game.

If the articles fail to download, try uninstalling your web browser and installing an earlier version.

If this fails disable ipv6 by editing /etc/sysctl.conf and adding the following lines to the end of the file.

net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1 net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 = 1 net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6 = 1

If ipv6 is still not disabled, then the problem is that sysctl.conf is still not activated. To solve this, type the command,

sudo sysctl -p

You will see this in the terminal:

net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1

net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6 = 1

net.ipv6.conf.lo.disable_ipv6 = 1

After that, if you run:

cat /proc/sys/net/ipv6/conf/all/disable_ipv6

It will report:

1

If you see 1, ipv6 has been successfully disabled.

If you still can't read the articles, make sure you changed line 141 of /etc/techringer.conf to reflect the number of moles on your neighbor's left testicle and have recompiled the kernel.
